label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Tolu, me o 😂 I’m in Biology 100L now and Medicine and Surgery was what I applied for. JAMB 2025, I scored 251 and got offered Biology at a federal uni here in Lagos. So when you said you’ve been crying, I understood immediately. The day I saw Biology on my portal, I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t even eat. It’s funny small now but that day nothing was funny.

My mum was still telling people in church that I was studying Medicine for like two months after that. I had to beg her to stop because how will I be trying to make peace with my admission and somebody will greet me with “our doctor” every Sunday 😭 So please don’t feel somehow for being disappointed. You wanted something, you worked towards it, then you opened your portal and saw something else. It hurts.

Let me answer the transfer part properly, because that was also one of the first things I wanted to know.

**Transfer to Medicine is real, but it is NOT automatic.** What our level adviser told us is that you need a CGPA of at least **4.5 out of 5**, AND there must be space in Medicine. Those are two separate things. Getting the 4.5 doesn’t mean they must move you. You can meet the academic requirement and still be waiting on whether there is a place available.

According to our adviser, about six people were moved into Medicine from the whole faculty last year. She thinks over 40 people applied. I’m saying “according to our adviser” because I wasn’t there counting applications myself, and even she wasn’t giving us an exact number for everyone who applied. But you can see why “just enter and transfer” is not something anybody should promise you.

She also told us that you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs in JAMB and post-UTME too. So your 268 alone doesn’t establish that you’re eligible for transfer. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or your post-UTME score, so please check both. Don’t let anybody see 268 and tell you “you’re qualified, just get first class” without knowing the actual rules.

Before you pay or reject anything, please go to your own faculty/department and ask. Tell them plainly that you were offered Biology but originally applied for Medicine, and you want to know the current requirements for moving to MBBS after 100L. Ask whether Biology students can apply, the CGPA required, the JAMB and post-UTME requirements, how selection works when there are more qualified applicants than spaces, and when applications happen.

If they have the rules written somewhere official, even better. You have two weeks before the acceptance deadline, so use some of that time to find out. Please don’t base this decision on forum people, including me. I can tell you what we were told here; I cannot promise that your school does the same thing.

And about “just read hard” — favour, I understand what you mean, but it’s not that simple. My first-semester CGPA is **4.31**. Not 4.5. I’m still trying. I’m telling you that so you know I’m not speaking as somebody who has already transferred or somebody who has secured it and is waiting for them to announce my name. I’m inside the uncertainty too.

Our 100L courses include BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. It’s not Biology morning, afternoon and night. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people 😭 If you accept with transfer in mind, you have to take all your courses seriously, not only the ones that feel related to Medicine. That CGPA will include the courses you don’t like too.

There are practical expenses as well. My lab coat was ₦6,500, dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and practical manual was extra. Those are my own costs, not a quotation for your school, but let your people know that there will be things to buy beyond accepting the admission.

Now, is Biology bad? Honestly, no. I’m enjoying it more than I expected, especially genetics and cell biology. I entered with my mind still on Medicine, so I wasn’t exactly ready to start praising Biology. But actually doing the course has been different from sitting at home looking at the name on my admission portal.

Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted and I was fine. I remember being interested in what we were doing, and that was one of the first times I thought, “Wait, I actually like this thing.” It didn’t suddenly erase my Medicine plans, but it made me stop treating every Biology class like punishment for not getting my first choice.

That’s my experience though. You may enjoy it, you may not. I don’t want to sell Biology to you just because I’m there. But being disappointed that you didn’t get Medicine and Biology being a bad course are not the same thing.

Kingsley, saying transfer is a myth is not true based on what our adviser told us. But the opposite advice, that you should accept and just read hard, also leaves out plenty. Transfer exists; getting it is another matter. Please, Tolu, don’t accept Biology believing your stay there must end after 100L.

One question I think you should sit with is: **if the transfer doesn’t happen, would I still be willing to continue Biology?** You don’t have to love it today, especially while you’re still upset, but be honest with yourself about that possibility.

And rewriting is not wrong either. If Medicine is really what you want and you’re ready for another admission cycle, that is a choice you can make. Just don’t let anybody tell you staying home is automatically easy or that another attempt guarantees Medicine. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected Pharmacy to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she’s still at home. I’m not saying that to frighten you or predict your own result. Her situation just made me understand that “one year is nothing” is easier to type than to live sometimes.

Also ask yourself privately whether you want to study Medicine, or whether part of the pressure is wanting to be “doctor” for your parents. No insult intended at all. With the way families celebrate Medicine, it can be hard to separate your own wish from everybody else’s expectations. I’ve had to think about that too.

Please get the school’s actual rules first, then talk with your dad using that information. Not “transfer is impossible” and not “transfer is sure.”

You don’t have to pretend you’re happy right now. Cry if you need to, but eat something too, abeg. Whether you accept Biology or decide to rewrite, this admission result is not the end of your world. You still have choices, even if none of them feels straightforward tonight.
